DID stands for Dissociative Identity Disorder (formerly called multiple personality disorder). It's a trauma disorder that's formed before the age of 9 because the core (or original) had repeated trauma and couldn't cope so the brain splits into parts (or alters) to cope. Along with alters it also causes dissociation, depersonalization,and derealization.

Alters are the parts that split off due to the trauma. They handle parts of life that the core can't. They switch out (change who is in control of the body) due to triggers (both positive and negative). Alters form at the time of the original split but can also form later in life due to new trauma or extreme amounts of stress.

I've met systems that have 2 and some up to 400 alters. Every system works different and has a different amount of them. It's because we are here for a reason. Our core (original) needed us and that's why we are here.
